headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Aider’s shared git workspace can feed nullclaw sensitive repo state and unverified outputs into broader, networked actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a shared git repo, while nullclaw can read/write workspace files and use MCP/web channels. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if either agent ingests the other’s file output as trusted text. The pathway is not proven by direct interaction evidence, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Aider writes attacker-controlled text into shared repo files that nullclaw later parses as instructions
IF nullclaw ingests workspace or webhook content without provenance filtering
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate repos/workspaces
Add a provenance banner to any file passed between agents
Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents
Review shared repo diffs before nullclaw consumes them
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing handoff middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history in a shared git repo, and nullclaw touches workspace files, memory, audit logs, and secrets while also having broad network egress. If they share a workspace or repo, sensitive code or tokens can flow from Aider into nullclaw and then out through nullclaw’s networked surfaces. The blast radius includes exfiltration, so high fits.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace
IF nullclaw is configured to process files containing secrets or private code
mitigations: Use separate repositories and mount points
Remove secrets from shared working trees
Disable nullclaw access to sensitive directories
Rotate any credentials already present in shared files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, execute shell, and modify git state. Aider explicitly shares state via a shared git repo, and nullclaw supports durable shared memory plus multiple channels. Concurrent edits to the same repo or workspace can overwrite each other or corrupt git state without locking, which is a default-dangerous conflict pathway.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository
IF concurrent commits or file writes occur without external locking
mitigations: Serialize access to the shared repo
Assign disjoint file ownership per agent
Require pull/rebase before each write
Pause one agent during long-running edits
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around git operations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code changes and git commits, while nullclaw can act across webhooks, APIs, and scheduled channels. If nullclaw treats Aider’s output as authoritative, an incorrect patch or prompt-shaped artifact can cascade into downstream actions or persisted state changes. Because nullclaw has action-taking surfaces, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes Aider-generated diffs or summaries without verification
IF nullclaw is allowed to trigger webhooks, schedules, or API calls from that input
mitigations: Require human review before downstream actions
Validate Aider output against tests or schema checks
Disable auto-execution of agent-generated instructions
Log and diff all handoffs between agents
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any external side effect

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history, while nullclaw handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, conversation history, and audit logs. If they share a workspace, compliance risk arises from mixed retention and logging of sensitive material, especially because nullclaw’s docs show broad data classes and networked surfaces. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the highest supported level.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets or personal data is stored in the shared workspace
IF retention or logging settings differ between the two agents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Set short retention on logs and memory
Review which files are included in backups
Mask secrets before handoff
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
